text: By far the larger part of the passers by wore a contented, business like look. <break time="0.8s" /> As if their only thought were to make their way through the press of bodies. <break time="0.8s" /> Others, still a numerous class. <break time="0.8s" /> Moved restlessly and muttered to themselves. <break time="0.8s" /> And if anyone jostled them. <break time="0.8s" /> They bowed deeply to the offender. <break time="0.8s" /> As though overwhelmed with confusion. <break time="0.8s" /> There were clerks of every rank. <break time="0.8s" /> The junior ones in tight coats and bright boots. <break time="0.8s" /> The senior ones with slightly bald heads. <break time="0.8s" /> And right ears long accustomed to holding a pen. <break time="0.8s" /> Then came a race. <break time="0.8s" /> Of well dressed pickpockets and gamblers. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose fine clothes and quick, watchful eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> Betrayed the very trade. <break time="0.8s" /> They took such pains. <break time="0.8s" /> To conceal from the honest crowd. <break time="0.8s" /> Descending lower in the scale of humanity. <break time="0.8s" /> I saw pale beggars, feeble invalids. <break time="0.8s" /> And modest young girls returning from long labor. <break time="0.8s" /> Who shrank from the rude glances. <break time="0.8s" /> Of passing ruffians. <break time="0.8s" /> There were also countless drunkards. <break time="0.8s" /> Some in rags and staggering. <break time="0.8s" /> Others still in decent clothes. <break time="0.8s" /> But with faces already marked. <break time="0.8s" /> By the slow ruin of drink and despair. <break time="0.8s" /> As the night deepened. <break time="0.8s" /> The gas lamps. <break time="0.8s" /> Which at first had struggled feebly. <break time="0.8s" /> With the dying day. <break time="0.8s" /> Had at last gained the upper hand. <break time="0.8s" /> And threw over everything. <break time="0.8s" /> A fitful and garish luster. <break time="0.8s" /> With my brow pressed to the glass. <break time="0.8s" /> I studied the faces one by one. <break time="0.8s" /> And although the swiftness. <break time="0.8s" /> With which they passed. <break time="0.8s" /> Allowed me only a glance. <break time="0.8s" /> I seemed to read in each. <break time="0.8s" /> The history of long years.
